title: Introduce timebound operator roles, KMS escrow handshake, and retention-backed audit anchor
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: operator sessions are long-lived in some edge workflows and can be abused if an operator account is compromised. We need a minimal, deployable pattern that limits operator privileges to a configurable time window, ties temporary escalation to an auditable KMS-backed escrow handshake, and ensures audit logs are anchored to a retention policy that preserves non-repudiation for a minimum TTL. This PR implements a time-windowed RBAC extension (RBAC v2 schema additions), a KMS escrow flow for short-lived operator claims, and an audit anchoring component that stamps events with retention and escrow metadata.

Summary of changes: added new database migration and protobufs for timebound roles; new operator-session controller implementing request->approve->escrow flow; KMS escrow client that requests an ephemeral envelope, stores escrow proof alongside the operator session; audit-anchor service that adds retention TTL and escrow-hash into audit events and emits a signed anchor to the audit-forwarder pipeline. Small compat shim included for the rbac policy compiler to accept a time window on role bindings.

Checklist: 
- [x] RBAC model & migration 
- [x] KMS escrow client + integration tests (local KMS emulator) 
- [x] Audit anchor wiring + unit tests 
- [x] Policy compiler acceptance tests updated 
- [x] Docs: 'operator-timebound-roles.md' draft in docs/ (ready for review) 
- [x] Rollout plan and kill-switch added to operator controller config

Migration notes: new migration rbac_timebound_roles_v1 adds two tables: operator_sessions and escrow_proofs. Existing role bindings are unaffected; default behaviour when time_window is absent remains unrestricted (backwards compatible). DBA timeline: this migration should run during maintenance window because it adds indexing on operator_id.

Rollout plan: feature gated by cluster config (rbac.timebound_enabled=false by default). Staged rollout: enable in staging for two weeks, enable in canary, then gradual ramp across regions. If KMS issues are observed, controller exposes fallback to deny new operator escalations and uses prior behaviour for existing sessions until issue resolved.

Testing/CI: unit and integration tests added. One CI job flaked (TestOperatorControllerRace) on first run and was retriggered and passed. Load test indicates ~2% p99 latency increase on operator-check path when timebound checks are enabled; batching improvements for the policy compiler in a follow-up will mitigate.

Security considerations: KMS escrow uses envelope encryption and signs a proof hash that is stored in escrow_proofs. Proofs are hashed and HMAC'd with a cluster-level audit key. Access to the audit-anchor endpoint is RBAC protected and audited. We added rate limits to the escrow handshake to limit operator enumeration.

Related work: builds on ENG-1120 (rbacv2 schema) and SEC-35 (audit retention requirements). Linear tickets ENG-1284 and SEC-77 track follow-ups: telemetry for escrow usage and automated expiry reclaim.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the KMS integration small and uses the existing kms/client interface; a wider multi-provider fallback will be added in a follow-up to avoid expanding scope in this change.

release_notes: Add timebound operator roles with KMS-backed escrow for short-lived operator claims, and introduce audit anchoring that records escrow metadata and retention TTL. Feature is feature-gated and off by default. See docs/operator-timebound-roles.md for migration and rollout instructions.
notes_for_ops: DB migration must run during maintenance window. Ensure cluster KMS credentials present in secret 'cluster-kms-escrow'. If any KMS errors are observed, flip rbac.timebound_enabled=false and restart operator-controller pods.
audit_impact: Audit logs now include escrow_proof_hash, escrow_provider, and retention_ttl fields. Audit-forwarder will index the anchor signature to enforce retention compliance.
